summary: On remote Luminara, a Verge family boards a working grain freighter as civilian migrants bound for more prosperous Auric. Its Verge-owned food shipment will move under Fleet escort through the newly reblazed high-speed Green Corridor, exposing both trade and passengers to raids.
settingText: LUMINARA FIELDS — VERGE AGRICULTURAL FREIGHT DOCK — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: LUMINARA FIELDS — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Dock Worker
dialogueInline.text: Local reserves stay sealed. The Auric load goes on this freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Keep hold of your bag. The passenger line's moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Will Auric have better rooms than here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: That's what we're going to find out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Are the Shards going to stop the ship?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: The escorts know the crossing. Come on.

panelPlan: Warm morning on Luminara: a productive but remote Verge farming world, intact agricultural loaders, grain silos and a modest civilian passenger gate serving the same long tan-green freighter. Cargo ownership remains with Verge growers and traders; no Fleet purchasing or requisition.

At the loading gantry, dock crews secure local reserve bins and load the trade allocation into visibly numbered-but-unlettered holds. A worker watches the route departure bulletin. Show distinct household food and outbound shipment; neither is being seized by Fleet.

The mother and boy carry practical personal bags, a moving bundle and tickets through a separate pedestrian boarding lane. Their departure for Auric is an intentional relocation, not an invented official assignment to grain logistics.

At a passenger viewport the boy watches familiar fields and grain containers. The mother checks their berth ticket and winter clothing, balancing the promise of a prosperous hub with worries about a hazardous crossing.

Final wide: the same freighter departs with civilian passengers and agricultural cargo. A Verge escort and a distant Fleet protective cruiser await at route assembly; all are physically separate vehicles.
directionInline: Grain remains Verge-owned on Verge–Verge and Verge–Core routes; Fleet protects the shipment and gains authority through lasting route support, not through purchasing grain.
The mother and boy are civilian migrants leaving remote Luminara for more prosperous Auric. They do not work for Fleet or magically arrive on a different vessel.
Track the same grain freighter, passenger space, clothing and emergency gear through the raid and arrival. Civilian experience grounds the political stakes.

summary: The newly reblazed Green Corridor gives the convoy a dramatically faster crossing after generations of slow interstellar travel. At a slower Kaldr approach section, Naomi must share protection with Thunderbreak without surrendering Verge navigation authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: KALDR RIFT — GREEN CORRIDOR APPROACH

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Last beacon's green. Timing agrees across the line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Ride the inversion to the exit mark. Then slow the convoy before the wreck field.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak wants the exposed flank.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Give them room. Verge traffic control keeps the crossing order.

panelPlan: Start with the measurable high-speed transit environment: spacecraft riding a favorable reciprocal-field inversion inside a verified narrow low-tension volume, beacon references and instrument timing, not a supernatural glowing tunnel.

Show a controlled deceleration/exit into the Kaldr approach region. Wreckage and drift markers matter only once the convoy has transitioned to lower relative speed; the long grain freighter is still identifiable.
In Naomi's tan-green Verge cockpit Second compares beacon verification and time drift. Naomi gives spacing orders informed by local crossing practice.
Thunderbreak takes a separate protective flank at sensible relative distance. The cruiser is old, capable, and maintains the established hull silhouette.
End on an obscured cutter contact near the slow approach geometry. No high-speed corridor dogfight, impossible contact, or instantaneous positional change.
directionInline: Fleet escorts are militarily powerful; Verge pilots retain local route knowledge and want to control their own traffic. This is a conflict of jurisdiction and need, not mere dislike.
Keep trackable positions for lead freighter, escorts, Thunderbreak, wreck mass and possible incoming raiders. Debris has drift and requires continuous survey.
No unexplained labels on cockpit screens or background hulls.

summary: Naomi spots evidence of a planned cargo interception: the Shards know the convoy's exact route. She holds formation while Fleet screens the threatened grain freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: something is behind that wreck. Are we detecting Shard ships?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Almost like they knew we were coming. How?

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: The fleet is telling us to fall behind the Thunderbreak

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Oh? They’re not asking this time? Tell them we know this approach better than they do. so they can kiss our flank

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: captain sol says she’s staying in the lead, -please- protect us from the rear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Two contacts accelerating. They're not after the escort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Warn the cargo master. Seal the holds now.

panelPlan: Opening widescreen cockpit-view panel establishes the geometry already seen: compact raider contacts aligned against the identifiable grain freighter, with Thunderbreak protecting the convoy's open flank.

Naomi and Second compare drift and encounter timing at real working consoles. Her braid and brow scar match her approved identity; the second officer is visibly distinct and contributes decisions rather than asking rhetorical questions.
Close inserts reveal maneuver markers instead of predictive essays: two raider vectors converging on a freighter's service/docking fittings.

Naomi remains at her flight controls while Second relays her refusal to Fleet over a working transmitter, diplomatically requesting rear protection. Thunderbreak begins easing aft from its prior exposed-flank position without jumping across the convoy. As two cutters accelerate toward the cargo holds, Second reports them, Naomi orders the holds sealed, and Second transmits the cargo warning while the convoy adjusts speed.
End on exterior: Shard cutters emerge from wreck cover toward the grain freighter's cargo holds; Fleet reacts but cannot be everywhere along the approach.
directionInline: Nobody yet knows which individual supplied the raiders with the crossing window; Naomi infers only that the raid was informed.
Keep Venn's cruiser a protective presence, not a vessel that can instantaneously teleport between freighters.
Dialogue must reflect flight decisions and a developing situation. Avoid abstract confidence or thematic self-repetition.

summary: At Kaldr's slow approach, cutters from Abby's and Billie's independent Shard crews close on the Verge grain freighter. Thunderbreak is still guarding the convoy from aft and cannot intercept both cutters in time. Venn uses a nearby derelict to disrupt their approach, knowingly scraping her cruiser's port bow. One cutter veers away; the other stays on course for the cargo collar. Neither side deliberately targets passengers.
settingText: KALDR RIFT — CONVOY INTERCEPTION / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Two cutters breaking cover. Both heading for the grain ship's cargo collars.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: We're too far aft to block them. That wreck's just off our port bow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Match its drift. Bring our port bow alongside and ease it into their path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: We'll scrape the plating.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Damage control, stand by. Helm, take us in.

panelPlan: Opening wide continues the actual relative geometry from RF_I01_P03: the long tan-and-muted-green Verge grain freighter proceeds behind Naomi's leading escort; Thunderbreak is aft and offset toward the freighter's starboard side, following Second's request for rear protection. Two compact gray-white Shard cutters with red markings have emerged from wreck cover and are closing on the grain ship's starboard cargo collars. A substantial broken derelict lies near Thunderbreak's port-forward side, beside the cutters' constrained approach lane. Give all objects consistent headings and believable separation.

On Thunderbreak's broad, older, maintained navy-and-gold bridge, a distinct tactical officer reports the cutters' actual target. A duty officer establishes why Thunderbreak cannot overtake the attackers from its aft position. Venn, silver-streaked hair in her low bun and established navy Fleet uniform, makes a practical decision from her command station. Show real crew work at actual stations, not heroic posing or floating magical displays.

A narrow unlettered tactical insert or clear exterior angle establishes the maneuver before contact: Thunderbreak matches the derelict's relative drift and adjusts slightly toward it. The port-forward armor will brush the wreck's outer structure, imparting a modest lateral motion into the cutters' narrow approach lane. The freighter stays clear of both hulls. Do not imply instantaneous wreck displacement, invented tractor action, or a high-speed ram.

The dominant exterior action panel shows the same derelict shifting gradually across the nearer cutter's intended line as Thunderbreak's port bow makes a controlled glancing contact. Local metal scraping, short sparks, small debris, and a clearly bounded gouge on the port-forward plating show the deliberate cost. Preserve the established Thunderbreak silhouette and scale. No ship-wide blast or catastrophic collision.

Finish with the tactical result at comprehensible scale: one Shard cutter must break outward to avoid the drifting wreck, while the second cutter, already on the inside line, continues alongside the grain freighter toward its cargo collar, enabling the boarding on RF_I01_P05. In a compact closing visual rather than another redundant wide strip, show the same damaged port-bow section or a purely graphical damage-control indication. The civilian passenger compartment remains intact and no fatalities occur.
directionInline: Carry the same convoy from RF_I01_P03: Naomi's Verge escort leads, the identifiable Luminara freighter remains a single ship with its grain containers and passengers aboard, and Thunderbreak is aft on rear protection rather than appearing instantly between the freighter and cutters. The convoy has already slowed for Kaldr's wreck field; use low relative speeds and correct momentum throughout.

Abby and Billie command separate, cooperating Shard crews under standing Confederacy grain-raiding policy. Venn's bridge crew sees threatening cutters, not the captains or the source of the leaked crossing window. Do not introduce Abby or Billie into this page as visible characters or assume Fleet knows who supplied the route information.

The maneuver must produce only the intended result: a controlled port-forward armor scrape on Thunderbreak, enough derelict drift to force one cutter off line, and an unobstructed second cutter that can attach at the freighter's cargo collar next page. Carry the same scrape into RF_I01_P05, RF_I01_P06 and later appearances until repaired. No unexplained hull deformation or instant repairs.

This is a deliberate grain theft, not a planned assault on passengers. The cargo remains Verge-owned. Boarding causes limited collateral pressure trouble on RF_I01_P05, and the raiders later capture three grain containers while a separate container is damaged; none of that has happened yet on this page. Do not show fatalities or invent early cargo loss.

Use restrained Fleet navy/gold against Verge tan/green and Shard industrial gray-white/red, clear readable silhouettes and natural lighting. Only the five scripted dialogue lines are readable: no interface labels, hull writing, expository captions or invented text. Balloon tails must identify Tactical, Officer and Venn correctly. Compose a varied portrait comic layout with a dominant action panel, not five repetitive full-width strips.

summary: A Shard boarding cutter attaches to the grain freighter's cargo collar. A limited pressure leak and armed entry frighten the civilian migrants, but the raiders focus on grain and a Verge shipboard guard secures the passenger compartment. No one dies.
settingText: GRAIN FREIGHTER — ACCESS COMPARTMENT BESIDE CARGO HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: GRAIN FREIGHTER — PASSENGER ACCESS

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Keep still. I need the helmet seal closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Are they taking the grain?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. Stay behind this door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Cargo hold only. Leave the passengers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Verge Guard
dialogueInline.text: Passenger section's sealed. Stay clear of the cargo hatch.

panelPlan: Passenger presence is already established by boarding on story page 1. Re-establish one clear access cross-section: the freighter's transfer collar and grain stacks connect to a separate civilian passenger alcove, emergency pressure door and the Verge shipboard security team already assigned as convoy passenger protection.

Clear cross-section spatial logic: one freight access/collar, grain stacks and secured cargo hatches, a distinct passenger access alcove, emergency pressure door and the Verge security detail already stationed with the convoy's protected passengers.

A Shard boarding cutter attaches at the cargo collar; local cutting and a short pressure leak disturb straps and loose cloth. Do not depict endless decompression, uncontrolled zero gravity or randomly flying bodies.
At ground-level human scale, the mother seats the boy in an emergency helmet and checks the neck seal while shielding him with her own body. He stays a protected civilian, not a combat actor.

A raider orders a crew member toward cargo, while a Verge guard on the freighter's shipboard Verge guard directs civilians behind the sealed passenger door. Maintain distinguishable adult uniforms and grounded poses.
End with an external view or pressure-seal indicator showing that the passenger door holds while the grain holds remain contested; the family is not presented as magically evacuated.
directionInline: Passenger presence, security pre-positioning and compartment topology must be established before contact. Do not imply Fleet troops arrived through an unexplained teleport or docking event.

The child's fear concerns the family grain and immediate danger; adults respond with task-specific dialogue. The Shard raider acts under cargo-seizure orders, while potential collateral danger remains a genuine consequence of the attack.
No visible injury to the child. No gravity or suction spectacle unsupported by this compartment's pressure state.

summary: The Shard cutters escape with three intact grain containers while one of the freighter's remaining containers is damaged and spills cargo. Venn holds the defensive screen instead of pursuing, and Naomi shepherds the surviving freighter, passengers and cargo toward Auric. No fatalities.
settingText: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / KALDR RIFT — CONVOY AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: One cutter's clear with the grain. We could catch them if we leave the freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Hold position. Keep the damaged cargo collar inside our shield.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: The cutter will be out of range in forty seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Let it go. Give Sol a safe course out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Passenger pressure's holding. We've got a split grain container. I'll escort them to Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I'll stay on their flank.

panelPlan: Exterior establishes two concurrent facts: one raider cutter escaping behind moving wreckage, while the identifiable grain freighter has a damaged grain container and local hull/pallet damage from boarding action. Grain grains and cargo fragments drift into space in quantities appropriate to the breach.
On Thunderbreak command, an officer offers a credible short firing window, but doing so would move defensive coverage off the grain ship; the choice has an observable spatial cost.
Venn refuses pursuit with a practical protective order and assigns the passengers and compromised cargo to a safer path.

Naomi's smaller escort maneuvers beside the compromised freighter; an operational check confirms the passenger pressure seal still holds. The mother and boy remain in the passenger section; no impossible second evacuation is depicted.

Show a believable aftermath assessment: intact containers continue under escort, some grain is lost to space or fire and three intact containers have been taken by raiders. Distinguish captured, destroyed and surviving cargo rather than treating all as 'lost'.

Final wide image shows diminished but moving convoy in certified passage, Thunderbreak's damaged port bow plainly visible, and the attacking cutter's diminishing engine trace. Victory is partial and no triumphant pose replaces the civilian loss.
directionInline: Record distinct outcomes: three Verge grain containers were captured and delivered to Shard communities, feeding households there; a separate container ruptured, destroying some grain. Verge merchants bear the theft and future trade may be delayed. No deaths or invented cargo tonnages.

Venn's first choice spent cruiser armor to block the attackers; her second choice preserves civilian protection but permits a raider to escape. Those are distinct decisions with distinct consequences.
Fleet personnel and Naomi only know what their instruments or observed events support. The identity of the route-information source remains unknown to them.

summary: Auric receives the grain freighter and all its passengers alive. Three containers were seized, a separate container was ruptured, and surviving grain must be counted. The Luminara mother and son arrive to discover that a radiant hub can still be crowded and cold.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVAL BERTH AND CASUALTY STATION — EVENING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Three containers taken. One split. No one lost from the freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Keep the damage report with the Verge cargo manifest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: It's bigger than the pictures.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: It is. Let's find where we're sleeping.

panelPlan: Auric revealed in splendid scale: beautiful illuminated rings, trading docks and confident Verge civic design. The same freighter docks at a plausible berth, with Thunderbreak visible outside at a distance and its port-bow scrape intact.

Workers physically separate the damaged grain container from surviving intact Verge-owned cargo. Three missing container slots tell the theft story; the ruptured container tells the accidental-loss story. No casualty list or memorial.
Passengers disembark alive through a connected gangway, including the mother and boy. Dock staff direct them toward registration and crowded warming areas, with luggage from Luminara.
Venn and Naomi exchange a practical damage/accounting report with dock personnel; nobody claims the grain belongs to Fleet or invents fatalities.
In a striking contrast, the boy admires the radiant station through spotless glazing while the mother notices an overcrowded shelter queue and a resident shivering near an inadequate heater.
directionInline: All passengers from Luminara reached Auric alive. The mother and boy are relocating to a better-off station and discover that its beautiful architecture coexists with crowding and inadequate heat. Do not invent mourners or casualties.
Track the three seized containers separately from the damaged container; grain that reaches Shard homes is not destroyed.

summary: Halev, Auric's elected civilian leader and head of the Verge governing council, handles the immediate cost of lost Verge grain while new migrants arrive to discover limited shelter and heat. Fleet has no ownership claim on the cargo.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — PUBLIC GRAIN BERTH / CIVIC DESK — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Count what's actually docked. No distribution promises until we know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Three containers stolen and another spoiled. Traders at both ends of the route will feel that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Fleet protected the ship. It didn't insure the cargo.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: We came here because there'd be room to work and live.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: There will be places to register tonight. I won't tell you the queues are short.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: And the out-ring's heating allotment is already behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the civic warming room. I'll take the council complaints in the morning.

panelPlan: Auric's shining public freight concourse opens into crowded registration and ration desks, showing a prosperous working station under tangible pressure, not a ruined refugee camp.
Halev works directly with Verge manifests, Wallace's market commitments and Naomi's cargo-loss count; the grain is owned by Verge traders and communities, not Fleet.
The mother and boy arrive among other individual new residents carrying belongings. Staff try to direct them toward accommodation while heating capacity and berths are visibly stretched.

Halev authorizes a temporary local distribution priority and additional warming space within Auric's civilian jurisdiction; he does not issue orders to Fleet crews or claim to govern all independently owned Verge shipments.
End on a complete but smaller grain delivery passing under radiant architecture while a line of arriving residents waits for room assignments.
directionInline: Fleet wants permanent connection and escort authority, not ownership of grain. Auric and the wider Verge have their own elected political institutions and retain their cargo and civil commercial decisions.
Do not reduce Wallace to a comic-relief cynic. His contract and price concerns are legitimate, even where they conflict with humanitarian priorities.
Any ledger or interface may show simple abstract figures, but no unscripted words or numbers.

summary: Jex meets Billie privately after deliberately leaking crossing times and escort movements. He believed the Shards would skim grain without damaging the trade they need, and still thinks he can gain favors and influence on all sides; Billie reminds him that independent captains make their own decisions.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — TRADE CORRIDOR / DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I gave you the crossing time. Not a promise the freighter would come back in pieces.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Venn moved a wreck across our approach. The three we took are intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Now merchants are delaying the next run.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And our families are eating tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Which is why I thought you'd want the route open next week.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I do. But you can't steer every captain with a favor, Jex.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: No. I can usually get them to pick up when I call.

panelPlan: At a busy Auric market side passage, Jex quietly reviews physical shipping schedules and current freight accounts. Background traders are real people conducting business, not an intelligence lair.
Billie enters in established pale-gray/red Shard flight wear, vivid red hair and the posture of a familiar but independent captain. Their meeting is dangerous precisely because they know each other.

A small exchange of route timing data and a returned favor token makes the relationship legible. Jex did not direct a cargo seizure or specify containers: he sold or leaked information that made a raid possible.
Jex notices the damaged shipment and delayed crossings on the same board; the risk to future Verge and Shard supplies is an unwanted consequence of his game.
Billie leaves without a threat of mass civilian violence. Jex takes a different incoming trader call and continues negotiating, convinced influence and favors can still manage the problem.
directionInline: Jex knowingly leaked real convoy timing, routes and ship movements, expecting the Shards to skim cargo without collapsing commerce. He never arranged or commanded specific container transfers. He gains reciprocal favors and influence with all sides, but cannot control independent captains.

Billie and Abby carried out the Triarch's existing raiding order; the raid was not invented by Jex. Jex supplied crossing intelligence with expectations he could not enforce. Billie has real historical grievances and may interpret the damage as proof of Fleet aggression.

Jex's involvement is known to him and Billie, not to Fleet or Auric officials. His motives combine profit and a serious wish to prevent Shard civilians from starving. Dialogue remains practical and attributable.

summary: Three captured grain containers reach Black Drift and are distributed to real Shard households. Ashfang's damaged collar requires repair. The raiders took Verge resources, not annihilated them; Abby, Billie and Tessa remain close collaborators with emerging differences in priorities.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD REPAIR YARD — FOLLOWING SHIFT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — FOLLOWING SHIFT

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's port collar is torn through. We can patch it, but not before the next shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Unload the grain first. Families are waiting at the ration point.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: We got three containers past Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: And lost the others when the hold broke. That wasn't all Fleet's doing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Three containers won't last. We need merchants willing to make the next crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I want enough that our people won't be waiting on their next convoy.

panelPlan: Exterior of Black Drift, a working inhabited Shard industrial settlement. The angular, named Ashfang Marauder matches its approved hull precisely, with a visibly damaged docking/cargo collar matching the attack and approach.

Repairers tend Ashfang's damaged collar in a safe working bay while separate crews unload exactly three sealed captured containers. Shard civilians receive rations as individuals: a parent, older workers and neighbors taking supplies home. No child is placed in machinery or danger.

Tessa in compact flight clothing and silver-gray curls inspects the collar and predicts limited repair time; Abby tall, Black, braided and still, directs grain to ration crews rather than posing above them.
Billie reports her tactical success with energy and anger. Tessa ties material loss to the damaged hold without portraying herself as an uninvolved moral judge; she participated in Shard command.
End with Abby and Billie holding different priorities in a work bay: upcoming trade crossings versus forcing Fleet attention. Neither declares a final split.
directionInline: Shard repair yards are competent, maintained, lived-in industrial spaces; workers and civilians have individual lives. Never use skulls, spikes or barbarian raider cues.

The three stolen containers supply actual Shard households while Verge communities lose that same grain. Ruptured cargo, repairs and deterred future voyages add real net costs; do not claim all supplies simply vanished.
Abby and Tessa are sisters; preserve the established distinct visual identities and let shared familiarity inform their reactions without turning the page into explanatory genealogy.

summary: Abby works with Billie and Tessa to balance captured grain distribution against the repairs their independent crews need. Her influence arises from skill and trust, not formal authority over Billie's ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dock Worker
dialogueInline.text: The ration crew wants the last container now. If we stop repairs, Ashfang misses the convoy after next.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Use the cargo lift while the weld cools. Keep the pressure frame braced until Tessa signs it off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: That frame goes back under load too soon, the collar tears open again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Another crossing means another Fleet ship between us and dinner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then we need the collar intact and enough grain left for people who can't board a cutter.

panelPlan: Abby's earned influence with cooperating crews is visible amid labor: cargo lift, mechanical braces, pressure-frame repair and waiting ration workers occupy coherent positions in the hangar.
A frustrated adult dock worker argues over which task has priority, with a real concern about the next potential food delivery.

Abby reassigns lift work and directs the repair sequence so ration distribution and structural repair can continue without needless risk. Cooperating crews respond because they trust her practical judgment, not because Billie is her subordinate.
Tessa tests the braced collar and challenges premature release; she and Abby exchange an experienced sibling glance or abbreviated response grounded in shared practical history.
Billie objects to the necessity of another dangerous seizure. Her anger at ongoing scarcity is visible in how she watches hungry people receive small shares.
Conclude with a working lift delivering grain to the ration point while Ashfang's collar remains in repair; no wrestling, impossible throws or ceremonial slogan.
directionInline: The disagreement is among competent Shard adults under real pressure. Abby is not infallible and Billie is not a manic caricature.
An anonymous dock worker may speak without receiving an invented proper name. The physical repair and cargo movements must remain consistent panel to panel.
Billie's desire to make Fleet answer for historical harms should be shown through her focus on who imposes the shortages, not an abstract threat to civilians.

summary: In private, the three close friends assess the raid's short-term success and its cost to future trade. Abby tentatively wonders whether their settlements might receive supplies without a raid, knowing this would challenge Shard identities. Billie disagrees without treating her as an enemy; Tessa shares responsibility for the raiding life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's collar survived your landing. Barely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: It survived. Three containers made it home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: And two traders just pushed their next departures back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: We may end up repairing the same hole for an empty dock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: What if they could bring a share here without us intercepting them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And thank Fleet for letting us eat? That's a hard bargain to sell.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I didn't say I could sell it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: Good. I've still got an actual collar to fix. Hand me that brace.

panelPlan: An intimate repair-deck meal for Abby, Billie and Tessa, whose familiarity and shared work should be visible before disagreement. Practical charts and damaged equipment remain nearby, not a lecture-room holotable.
Tessa works on a collar seal with the sisters-in-arms trading small dry observations about repairs and how little grain three containers actually provide.

Abby notes delays in coming merchant crossings and quietly tests a possibility of legitimate delivery to their settlements. This is a private, uncomfortable speculation, not a public political platform.
Billie resists without cruelty: voluntary gifts from Fleet-protected traders sound like depending on the people who abandoned them. Her anger has real cultural roots.
End on all three resuming shared work and an ordinary friendly gesture despite tension. Their rupture is not yet underway.
directionInline: Every dialogue turn responds to a concrete proposal, constraint or objection. Abby, Billie and Tessa retain distinct operational goals and personal relationships.

Abby and Billie both believe Shards should not have to raid to survive. Abby is beginning to imagine receiving supplies voluntarily; Billie sees punitive coercion as a route to supplies and historical reckoning.
Abby and Tessa's sister relationship and Billie's bond with Tessa underlie the disagreement without explicit family-history exposition.

summary: The Silent Triarch confirms the confederation's standing grain-raid policy. The independent captains remain politically answerable to their communities and to the Triarch's influence, rather than serving a single shipboard chain of command. Abby argues that destroyed trade weakens the Shards without openly advocating reform.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raid
dialogueInline.text: The standing grain order remains. Our cutters take what the frontier carries.

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade
dialogueInline.text: Two merchants have suspended crossings since Kaldr. Fewer ships mean fewer supplies for us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear
dialogueInline.text: Fleet will protect every hold unless protection becomes expensive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: The damaged shipment cost us as well. I can intercept cargo. I can't make merchants replace wrecked ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raid
dialogueInline.text: Then ensure the next interception brings food home intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade
dialogueInline.text: Keep the traders willing to sail. We need their routes open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear
dialogueInline.text: And make the Core understand those routes are not theirs alone.

panelPlan: Establish exact chamber geography: Abby stands in a working Shard political command space before the three rulers seated in distinct fixed positions. Raid has a jagged dark-industrial mask, Trade a pale etched mask, Fear a smooth dark mask; positions stay invariant across views.
Material evidence—grain from the recent interception and a simple representation of delayed civilian commerce—is present on a practical shared table, not a mystical artifact.
Each member responds to a real consequence. Raid maintains an already-existing order; Trade worries about supply erosion; Fear interprets the engagement as a way to impose political pressure.
Abby challenges the practical impossibility of maintaining shipments by destroying the ships. Her composed body language indicates she is negotiating within authority she still recognizes.

The Triarch debates competing raiding strategies and future supply limits; disagreement remains political rather than a supernatural decree. End with Abby leaving with conflicting obligations, no invented oath or ceremonial speech.
directionInline: All three Triarch masks and political positions remain distinct and materially established. Do not invent hierarchy under which Abby commands Billie.
Confederation legitimacy rests on culture, scarcity, reputation and negotiated cooperation. Abby does not publicly advocate replacing raids with voluntary supplies in Issue 1.
Triarch and captains recognize that captured Verge grain is food for Shard households, while damage and reduced trade diminish future options.

summary: At Auric, Halev and his council allies confront the contrast between a radiant, prosperous hub and existing crowded, cold housing. The Green Corridor promises rapid commerce and relocation, and will intensify both benefits and pressures. This political decision is distinct from the earlier dock inventory.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC GRAIN DESK — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Traders who took months to reach us could make regular runs. That changes everything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Including how many ships we have to bring safely through the approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We already have new arrivals sleeping beside the heat vents.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The corridor will bring customers and workers. We need both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And those workers need somewhere warm to sleep. Send the housing figures to the council before we promise more berths.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I'll give you the route conditions. Don't sign away Verge traffic control to get an escort.

panelPlan: Morning Auric: exquisite inhabited ring architecture alongside real heated and unheated residential zones, crowded civilian queues, well-kept infrastructure and busy commerce. Avoid portraying the Verge hub as shabby.
Halev moves from the dock toward public shelter and heating plans with Wallace and Naomi; decisions are about long-term arrival capacity, not a repeat of the previous evening's grain tally.
A resident shows that comfortable private space cannot simply be reassigned; a migrant family waits with their belongings. Both have understandable needs.
Wallace explains the commercial advantage of new fast passages, while Naomi distinguishes protecting an approach from handing over civilian traffic authority.
Halev instructs the Verge council office to draft conditions for Fleet patrol support and local control, aware that more traffic means more pressure on Auric's finite warm rooms.
directionInline: Auric is genuinely radiant and economically desirable, yet already strained by crowded shelter and finite heating capacity. The new much-faster corridor promises greater trade and more relocation, accelerating both issues.
This is a strategic capacity discussion distinct from the damaged-grain count on P08. Show Halev's dual mandate as Auric's elected leader and chair of the Verge governing council.
Keep the earlier freighter, container count and Thunderbreak damage consistent without resetting the prior action.

summary: Halev, elected leader of Auric and chair of the wider Verge governing council, proposes a provisional Green Corridor arrangement: Verge civil traffic control and independent commerce, Fleet engineering verification, beacon upkeep, protective patrols and authority over its own ships. A durable route would be enormously valuable and politically consequential.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC ROUTE TABLE / WORKING BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Our pilots know the inversion. Fleet can certify markers and keep the cutters off it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Once ships exit the fast segment, Verge traffic control takes the approach. That's not negotiable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Fleet patrols the route. We keep the ports, freight and civilian crossing order.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: They'll want a lasting assignment once trade depends on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then the council will have to decide what that costs. Send Venn the proposed terms.

panelPlan: Auric's functioning civic control room: wall view of verified high-speed corridor segments, low-tension geometry, beacon timing and slower berth approach; restrained practical interfaces only.

Naomi demonstrates Verge pilots' empirical route knowledge, including where the recently reblazed fast segment must be reverified. Fleet has genuine survey, beacon-marking and military patrol capabilities.
Wallace weighs newly reachable markets against port crowding, heating and the possibility of Fleet making its protection difficult to refuse later.

Halev formulates a limited proposal for council approval: Auric/Verge civil crossing order and grain ownership remain local; Fleet controls its patrols, supports measured beacon verification and does not administer Verge ports.
A working clerk transmits terms to Venn for Fleet authorization. This does not represent a unilateral treaty binding every Verge community.
directionInline: The corridor has two separate layers: a safe navigable volume verified through measurable reciprocal-field and drift behavior, and political permission for commercial traffic and escort service.
Halev offers access and cooperation, not submission. Fleet wants the connection because it strengthens Reach and Resolve and creates ongoing interdependence.
The argument concerns enforceable exchange terms, route access, escort protection and who retains authority over cargo and port traffic.

summary: Venn presents Auric's conditional fast-corridor proposal to the Admiralty. Dominion sees permanent route verification and patrols as genuine restoration of connection and a source of lasting Fleet authority; Venn shares the Core faith in Reach and Resolve while taking local civilian needs seriously.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CORE ADMIRALTY — AFTER AURIC'S PROPOSAL

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Kaldr's fast segment is holding verification. Auric offers crossing data and civilian approach control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then we have a chance to make a reopened route dependable. Patrols, maintained markers, regular service.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: Until every merchant assumes our cruiser will be there. That becomes an obligation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: An obligation worth accepting. Reach and Resolve means more than discovering a passage once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Auric's council wants the ports and freight under Verge authority. We can work with that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Bring me a trial plan the crews can sustain.

panelPlan: Bright mature Fleet Admiralty chamber with measured reciprocal-field transit geometry, verification status and a tactical operating plan; Dominion and Rhyne remain credible senior officers, Venn a committed Core commander.

Venn presents the newly reblazed high-speed route and Auric's limited proposal for local control and Fleet protection. The physical achievement of restoring fast travel is clear without an exposition lecture.
Dominion supports an ongoing patrol and beacon program sincerely: permanent reconnection would prevent desperate isolation and establish Fleet's institutional role.
Rhyne questions the resource commitment and political consequences of becoming indispensable to a Verge economy, without falsely casting Dominion as seeking civilian harm.
Venn commits to making the joint route workable. Her concern for what crews and civilians actually experience is professional judgment within Fleet tradition, not a rejection of that tradition.
directionInline: Reach and Resolve is Fleet's long-term reconstruction doctrine. Fleet believes building and controlling interstellar connections increases both civilization's stability and Fleet political influence; those motives coexist.
Do not attempt to explain the entire physics or history of the Shattering. Use only relevant physical route data and opposing human decisions.
All three Fleet officers have distinct faces, ages and uniforms. Keep the hearing's dais and floor display spatially consistent.

summary: Dominion authorizes a monitored Green Corridor trial with continued field verification, beacon maintenance and Fleet patrols. Auric retains civilian traffic and cargo control, subject to council agreement. The plan is both genuine public service and the beginning of lasting Fleet influence.
settingText: CORE ADMIRALTY CHAMBER — GREEN CORRIDOR AUTHORIZATION

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Authorize the Kaldr trial. Maintain the markers and deploy an escort once Thunderbreak is ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: A trial can become a permanent obligation faster than we can supply it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then we judge its value honestly. People have spent generations traveling the slow way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Port-bow repairs come first. Auric gets the written conditions before the next convoy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Agreed. Keep that route open if the measurements allow it.

panelPlan: Remain in the same Admiralty chamber. Dominion signs a concrete operational trial: verification checks, Fleet protection, clear approach jurisdiction and an Auric council review.
Venn points to Thunderbreak's port-bow damage and necessary repairs before a safe redeployment. Institutional care is operational rather than ceremonial.
Rhyne identifies the cost of maintaining the route long term: once a fast crossing becomes reliable, businesses and families may cease planning for the years-long slower alternatives.
Dominion remains convincing and principled: the ability to restore dependable movement is an accomplishment that merits continued service, not an overt plan to scare civilians.
Final framing centers approved beacon and patrol work. No magical portal imagery, unscripted interface text, or triumphant authority-over-civilians pose.
directionInline: The corridor is being opened because Dominion wants Reach and Resolve to proceed. He is not reluctantly surrendering a preference for isolation.
The practical and political approval are distinct: mapped transit geometry is measured; the agreement concerns access, escorts, jurisdiction and emerging dependence.
No invented legal text, route names or interface labels; the only readable text is prescribed dialogue and captions.

summary: News of continued high-speed passage and Fleet patrols reaches Black Drift. Abby, Billie and Tessa—close allies commanding within an independent-captain confederation—prepare for another cargo raid. More commerce may feed more Shard families, but continuing Fleet expansion sharpens their disagreement.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — AFTER THE KALDR AUTHORIZATION

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: The merchants are scheduling again. Gravefire's ready when you two are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: More crossings, more chances to bring grain home. Keep it intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And more Fleet guns watching every move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You don't need me to tell you what happened to Ashfang's collar.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: No. Tess has mentioned it once or twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: If you're both finished borrowing my tools, I'd like them back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Give her the tools, Billie. We've got ships to ready.

panelPlan: Wide Black Drift departure bay with physically coherent independent Shard vessels preparing under their own captains; Ashfang's collar is repaired enough for flight, with the repair history still visible.
Working crews report newly scheduled fast-corridor freight movements. More regular trade means more opportunities to feed Shard households, but also greater Fleet patrol presence.
Abby, Billie and Tessa share a relaxed moment of familiar practical work; show their long loyalty before an exchange about different tactical priorities.

Abby speaks about taking food without ruining merchant traffic. Billie believes the Core must feel pressure too; her view is expressed without pre-announcing the Issue 2 passenger-targeting escalation.
Close on separate ships departing from coherent docks, with no single captain commanding another's vessel and no visible formal breach among the three.
directionInline: Opening the connection serves Fleet's political aims and gives Shards new opportunities to obtain supplies. All three powers have something to gain and something to lose.

Billie favors coercive attacks partly as revenge for real generational harm, while Abby increasingly considers voluntary provision as a way beyond raiding; those trajectories are nascent, not completed in this issue.
The final hook is the operational and personal danger of two leaders interpreting the same opening corridor differently. Dialogue stays attributable and grounded in what they intend to do.
